propositions: The complexity lock compares branch baseline against main tip instead of merge-base, causing un-rebased branches to fail when main lowers a ceiling, falsely blaming the branch for a change main made
When main reduces a ceiling (e.g. 19→17), any open branch still carrying the pre-reduction baseline presents that old ceiling against main's new one, triggering a false 'RAISED ceiling' violation
The fix must compute merge-base(main, HEAD) and read the baseline at that commit, so only entries the branch itself changed can violate the lock
The CI fetch of main uses --depth=1 which is too shallow to compute a merge base, requiring the fetch to deepen or unshallow before retry
When merge base cannot be computed the gate must fall back to main-tip comparison (stricter, never looser) with an explicit note, preserving fail-closed posture
